claim: Saprolegnia parasitica is one of the most virulent oomycete species in freshwater aquatic environments.
source: Saprolegnia parasitica is one of the most virulent oomycete species in freshwater aquatic environments, causing severe saprolegniasis and leading to significant economic losses in the aquaculture industry.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the abstract without specific experimental data in this manuscript, drawing from general scientific knowledge.

claim: Saprolegnia parasitica causes severe saprolegniasis leading to significant economic losses in the aquaculture industry.
source: Saprolegnia parasitica is one of the most virulent oomycete species in freshwater aquatic environments, causing severe saprolegniasis and leading to significant economic losses in the aquaculture industry.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact drawing from general scientific knowledge about the impact of this pathogen.

claim: Linalool is a natural antibiotic alternative found in various essential oils.
source: Linalool, a natural antibiotic alternative found in various essential oils, exhibits promising antimicrobial activity against a wide range of pathogens.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about linalool's source and classification.

claim: Linalool exhibits promising antimicrobial activity against a wide range of pathogens.

claim: Linalool disrupted the cell membrane of S. parasitica mycelium, causing intracellular components to leak out.

claim: Linalool prohibited ribosome function, thereby inhibiting protein synthesis and ultimately affecting mycelium growth.
source: (2) Linalool prohibited ribosome function, thereby inhibiting protein synthesis and ultimately affecting mycelium growth.
evidence: This is supported by transcriptome analysis showing downregulation of ribosome biogenesis genes and molecular docking studies.

claim: Linalool enhanced the complement and coagulation system which in turn activated host immune defense and lysed S. parasitica cells.
source: (1) Linalool enhanced the complement and coagulation system which in turn activated host immune defense and lysate S. parasitica cells
evidence: This is supported by transcriptome data showing upregulation of complement and coagulation genes in treated fish.

claim: Linalool promoted wound healing, tissue repair, and phagocytosis to cope with S. parasitica infection.
source: (2) Linalool promoted wound healing, tissue repair, and phagocytosis to cope with S. parasitica infection
evidence: This is supported by histopathological observations and transcriptome analysis showing upregulation of relevant genes.

claim: Linalool positively modulated the immune response by increasing the abundance of beneficial Actinobacteriota.
source: (3) Linalool positively modulated the immune response by increasing the abundance of beneficial Actinobacteriota

claim: Linalool stimulated the production of inflammatory cytokines and chemokines to lyse S. parasitica cells.

claim: Saprolegniasis infects a wide host range including fish, crustaceans, amphibians, and their eggs.
source: Saprolegniasis is one of the most serious oomycete diseases in the aquaculture industry all over the world, infecting a wide host range (fish, crustaceans, amphibians, and their eggs) with a conspicuous symptom (grayish-white cotton wool-like covering on the surface of host) (Derevnina et al., 2016; Tandel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Derevnina et al., 2016 and Tandel et al., 2021.

claim: Saprolegniasis presents with a conspicuous symptom of grayish-white cotton wool-like covering on the surface of the host.
